what: Alert that new flood water appears on the next Sentinel-1 pass, from the largest 3-day rain total
threshold_rule: Published anchor, fixed before looking at our data: Camarasa-Belmonte (2016), J. Hydrol. 541, 99-115, doi:10.1016/j.jhydrol.2016.03.019
why_not_fitted: Only 4 new-flood labels in training, 3 after 7-29 mm of rain (water management or radar noise); the best-Peirce threshold then alarms on almost any rain. See metrics.json.
alert_rule: share of ECMWF ensemble members whose largest 3-day total in the next 3 days reaches the threshold: red >= 0.5, amber >= 0.1
rain_source: Open-Meteo: ECMWF IFS 9 km archive (history), IFS single runs (replay), ECMWF IFS 0.25 deg 51-member ensemble (live); site value = max over a 0.1 deg lattice
caveats: Gridded rain misses extremes: the IFS cell saw about 72 mm in the DANA, AEMET Pego 634 mm.
Few flood events since Aug 2024, so the threshold is loose and the probability is not calibrated.
The 100 mm anchor comes from station totals; ours is the wettest IFS grid point, a different product.
Local rain only: river water from upstream and sea surge (both mattered in 2024 and 2026) are not inputs.
Label = new water on the next radar pass; floods that drain between passes are missed.
